        b = next_id; next_id += 1
        c = next_id; next_id += 1
        p = next_id; next_id += 1
        q = next_id; next_id += 1
        r = next_id; next_id += 1
        # triangles
        edges += [(a,b), (b,c), (c,a)]
        edges += [(p,q), (q,r), (r,p)]
        # connections
        def lit_vertex(lit):
            if lit > 0:
                return var_pos[lit]
            else:
                return var_neg[-lit]
        v1 = lit_vertex(lits[0])
        v2 = lit_vertex(lits[1])
        v3 = lit_vertex(lits[2])
        edges += [(a, v1), (b, v2), (p, c), (q, v3), (r, F)]
    # normalize edges
    norm_edges = []
    seen = set()
    for u, v in edges:
        if u == v:
            continue  # should not happen
        if u > v:
            u, v = v, u
        if (u, v) not in seen:
            seen.add((u, v))
            norm_edges.append([u, v])
    return {"n": next_id, "edges": norm_edges}

"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT (ThreeSat) to 3-Coloring (ThreeColoring).

Colours are represented by three base vertices forming a triangle:
    T = 0, F = 1, B = 2
with edges (0,1), (1,2), (0,2).  These three vertices are pairwise adjacent so
they always receive three distinct colours; we use B as a fixed "reference"
colour and treat the other two as true/false.

Variable gadget for variable v:
    two vertices pos[v] and neg[v], with edges
        pos[v] -- neg[v]
        pos[v] -- B
        neg[v] -- B
    Since both are adjacent to B they cannot use B, and they are adjacent to
    each other, so they must take the two remaining colours, i.e. exactly one
    is T and the other is F.  pos[v] = T means v is true.

Clause gadget for clause (l1, l2, l3):
    three new vertices c1, c2, c3 forming a triangle (all pairwise adjacent),
    and edge ci -- (literal node of li).
    The three ci need three distinct colours.  If all literals are F, each ci
    is adjacent to an F vertex, so none can be F; they would have to use only
    {T, B}, impossible for a triangle.  If some li is T, set ci = F and colour
    the other two with T and B: this is always a proper colouring regardless
    of the remaining literals.  Hence the gadget is 3-colourable iff at least
    one literal is true.

The construction is linear in the input size, hence polynomial time.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    num_vars = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]

    # Base palette triangle: T=0, F=1, B=2.
    T, F, B = 0, 1, 2
    edges = [(T, F), (F, B), (T, B)]

    n = 3  # vertices 0,1,2 already used

    # Variable gadgets.
    pos = {}
    neg = {}
    for v in range(1, num_vars + 1):
        p = n
        q = n + 1
        n += 2
        pos[v] = p
        neg[v] = q
        edges.append((p, q))
        edges.append((p, B))
        edges.append((q, B))

    def literal_node(lit):
        if lit > 0:
            return pos[lit]
        else:
            return neg[-lit]

    # Clause gadgets.
    for clause in clauses:
        c1, c2, c3 = n, n + 1, n + 2
        n += 3
        # Triangle among the three clause vertices.
        edges.append((c1, c2))
        edges.append((c2, c3))
        edges.append((c1, c3))
        # Connect each clause vertex to its literal node.
        for c, lit in zip((c1, c2, c3), clause):
            edges.append((c, literal_node(lit)))

    return {"n": n, "edges": edges}

"""Polynomial-time reduction from 3-SAT (ThreeSat) to 3-Coloring (ThreeColoring).

Colours are represented by three base vertices forming a triangle:
    T = 0, F = 1, B = 2
with edges (0,1), (1,2), (0,2).  These three vertices are pairwise adjacent,
so they always receive three distinct colours; B is a fixed reference colour
and T/F are the truth colours.

Variable gadget for variable v:
    two vertices pos[v], neg[v] with edges
        pos[v] -- neg[v],  pos[v] -- B,  neg[v] -- B
    Both are adjacent to B, so neither can be B, and they are adjacent to each
    other, so they take the two remaining colours: exactly one is T and the
    other F.  pos[v] = T means v is true.

Not-all-equal (NAE) gadget for inputs (a, b, c):
    three new vertices x, y, z forming a triangle, with edges x--a, y--b, z--c.
    x, y, z need three distinct colours, and each x/y/z must avoid the colour
    of its input.  A system of distinct representatives exists iff the three
    input colours are not all equal (if they are all equal, only two colours
    remain for the triangle).  Hence this gadget is 3-colourable iff a, b, c
    are not all equal.

Clause gadget for clause (l1, l2, l3):
    introduce a fresh variable s (nodes ps, ns via the variable gadget) and add
        NAE(l1, l2, ps)   and   NAE(ns, l3, F)
    where F is the fixed false base vertex (colour 1).  This is satisfiable for
    some s iff l1 or l2 or l3 is true:
      * if l3 is true (colour 0), NAE(ns, 0, 1) holds for every s, and s can be
        chosen so that NAE(l1, l2, ps) holds;
      * if l3 is false (colour 1), NAE(ns, 1, 1) forces ns = 0 (s false), and
        then NAE(l1, l2, ps=1) holds exactly when l1 or l2 is true;
      * if all three literals are false, the second gadget is unsatisfiable.
    Conversely, a colouring of the graph yields truth values for the literal
    nodes, and the two NAE gadgets force at least one literal of the clause to
    be true.

The construction uses O(num_vars + num_clauses) vertices and edges, so it runs
in polynomial time.  No solver is called.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    num_vars = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]

    # Base palette triangle: T=0, F=1, B=2.
    T, F, B = 0, 1, 2
    edges = [[T, F], [F, B], [T, B]]
    n = 3  # vertices 0, 1, 2 already used

    pos = {}
    neg = {}

    def new_variable():
        """Add a variable gadget and return its (positive, negative) nodes."""
        nonlocal n
        p = n
        q = n + 1
        n += 2
        edges.append([p, q])
        edges.append([p, B])
        edges.append([q, B])
        return p, q

    for v in range(1, num_vars + 1):
        pos[v], neg[v] = new_variable()

    def literal_node(lit):
        if lit > 0:
            return pos[lit]
        return neg[-lit]

    def add_nae(a, b, c):
        """Triangle gadget, 3-colourable iff a, b, c are not all equal."""
        nonlocal n
        x = n
        y = n + 1
        z = n + 2
        n += 3
        edges.append([x, y])
        edges.append([y, z])
        edges.append([x, z])
        edges.append([x, a])
        edges.append([y, b])
        edges.append([z, c])

    for clause in clauses:
        l1, l2, l3 = clause
        ps, ns = new_variable()
        add_nae(literal_node(l1), literal_node(l2), ps)
        add_nae(ns, literal_node(l3), F)

    return {"n": n, "edges": edges}

```python
def reduce(instance):
    num_vars = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    T, F, B = 0, 1, 2
    edges = [(T,F),(F,B),(T,B)]
    n = 3
    pos = {}
    neg = {}
    def add_var():
        nonlocal n
        p = n; q = n+1; n += 2
        edges.append((p,q)); edges.append((p,B)); edges.append((q,B))
        return p,q
    for v in range(1, num_vars+1):
        pos[v], neg[v] = add_var()
    def lit_node(lit):
        return pos[lit] if lit>0 else neg[-lit]
    def add_nae(a,b,c):
        # triangle of 3 new vertices connected to a,b,c
        nonlocal n
        x,y,z = n, n+1, n+2; n += 3
        edges.append((x,y)); edges.append((y,z)); edges.append((x,z))
        edges.append((x,a)); edges.append((y,b)); edges.append((z,c))
    for clause in clauses:
        l1,l2,l3 = clause
        ps, ns = add_var()
        add_nae(lit_node(l1), lit_node(l2), ps)
        add_nae(ns, lit_node(l3), F)
    return {"n": n, "edges": edges}
```

def reduce(instance):
    num_vars = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]

    T, F, B = 0, 1, 2
    edges = [[T, F], [F, B], [T, B]]
    n = 3

    pos = {}
    neg = {}

    def new_variable():
        nonlocal n
        p = n
        q = n + 1
        n += 2
        edges.append([p, q])
        edges.append([p, B])
        edges.append([q, B])
        return p, q

    for v in range(1, num_vars + 1):
        pos[v], neg[v] = new_variable()

    def literal_node(lit):
        if lit > 0:
            return pos[lit]
        return neg[-lit]

    def add_nae(a, b, c):
        nonlocal n
        x = n
        y = n + 1
        z = n + 2
        n += 3
        edges.append([x, y])
        edges.append([y, z])
        edges.append([x, z])
        edges.append([x, a])
        edges.append([y, b])
        edges.append([z, c])

    for clause in clauses:
        l1, l2, l3 = clause
        ps, ns = new_variable()
        add_nae(literal_node(l1), literal_node(l2), ps)
        add_nae(ns, literal_node(l3), F)

    return {"n": n, "edges": edges}
```
